constitutional_basis: Article VIII (frozen criterion), Article XXVI (ACTUAL external solver), Article XXVIII (no semantic promotion)

experimental_design.thesis: P-19's distributed micro-shunt swarm maintains safer ICP than single-segment under obstruction because obstructing one of N channels reduces total conductance by 1/N, not to zero.
experimental_design.test_method: Use svMultiPhysics to simulate obstruction by increasing outlet resistance. Compare: (A) distributed (10 channels, 1 obstructed = 90% conductance remaining) vs (B) single (1 channel, obstructed = 10% conductance remaining). The flow rates represent the per-channel flow after obstruction.
experimental_design.frozen_metric: Inlet pressure (proxy for ICP). Distributed inlet pressure < single inlet pressure under obstruction.
experimental_design.frozen_threshold: Distributed inlet < 50% of single inlet under obstruction. Frozen BEFORE execution.

obstruction_modeling.distributed_obstructed: 10 channels, 1 fully obstructed. Effective flow = 9/10 of total. Each remaining channel carries 1/9 of total flow. Run svMultiPhysics at 0.111x flow (representing 1/9 per channel).
obstruction_modeling.single_obstructed: 1 channel, 90% obstructed. Effective conductance = 10%. Run svMultiPhysics at 0.1x flow BUT with 10x outlet resistance (simulating partial obstruction).
obstruction_modeling.note: The key difference: distributed loses 1/10 of channels (90% capacity), single loses 90% of one channel (10% capacity). The distributed architecture is supposed to maintain drainage while single collapses.

frozen_acceptance_criterion.pass: Distributed (9/10 channels) inlet pressure < 50% of single-obstructed (90% blocked) inlet pressure
frozen_acceptance_criterion.model_disagreement: If 3D result disagrees with 1D prediction by > 25%
frozen_acceptance_criterion.insufficient_resolution: If solver does not converge or mesh too coarse
